uncited: This separation allows the use of highly optimized, standard rasterization pipelines for the final image generation.
The core mechanism of IVR involves a two-stage pipeline: extraction and rendering.
**Extraction (Preprocessing):** The volumetric dataset is analyzed to identify regions of interest.
This is typically achieved by defining a threshold or a range of values.
The algorithm traverses the volume data to locate the boundary between the "inside" and "outside" of the target region.
This creates a surface mesh that approximates the isosurface defined by the threshold.
**Rendering:** The resulting geometric primitives are passed to the standard graphics hardware pipeline.
This approach extracts surfaces directly from the spatial domain of the volume data.
It is chosen when explicit surface geometry is required for interaction or when standard rasterization performance is prioritized over transparency effects.
It is less common for standard isosurface extraction and is typically used for specific spectral analysis or filtering tasks.
Indirect Volume Rendering emerged as a strategy to leverage the rapid advancements in standard 3D graphics hardware for scientific visualization.
By converting volume data into polygonal meshes, researchers could utilize the fixed-function pipeline of early GPUs.
